title: Impatient Bandits: Optimizing Recommendations for the Long-Term Without Delay

problem.claim: The paper studies content exploration for recommendation systems that seek to increase users' long-term satisfaction, formalized as a multi-armed bandit problem with delayed rewards.

gap.claim: Waiting for full long-term rewards slows learning, while short-term proxy rewards imperfectly reflect the long-term objective.

contributions.claim: A predictive model of delayed rewards incorporates all information obtained to date.
A Bayesian filter combines full observations with partial short- or medium-term outcomes to produce a probabilistic belief.
A bandit algorithm uses the predictive model to balance exploration and exploitation while learning which content aligns with long-term success.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report applying the approach to podcast recommendation to identify shows with repeated user engagement over two months.
The authors report substantially better performance than approaches optimizing short-term proxies or waiting for fully realized long-term outcomes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommendation systems are increasingly tasked with improving users' long-term satisfaction.
The work formalizes content exploration with delayed rewards and identifies a trade-off between delayed full rewards and imperfect short-term proxies.
The approach combines a delayed-reward predictive model, Bayesian filtering of full and partial outcomes, and a bandit algorithm.
The method is applied to podcast recommendation focused on repeated engagement over two months.
The authors report substantially better performance than short-term-proxy and fully delayed-reward alternatives.

source_observation.claim: Combining partial outcomes with full observations through a Bayesian filter produces a probabilistic belief about delayed rewards.

interpretation.claim: Intermediate signals can support learning before the final long-term outcome is available.

application.claim: Use models that integrate partial and complete feedback when optimizing objectives with delayed outcomes.

exception.claim: Short-term signals may not adequately represent the long-term objective.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the predictive model, Bayesian filter, or bandit algorithm in technical detail.
The abstract does not provide datasets, metrics, numerical results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not establish whether the reported performance was independently verified.
